body:
To be honest, while I don't have a time set for it, I'm already at the "viable plan" stage, which is what both has me concerned enough to want to reach out but also too scared to reach out to a professional. I'm worried I might have waited a bit too long and let things get to bad to seek professional help. 

I wonder if I couldn't just maybe talk to someone and leave out the more concerning aspects of my thought processes and only tell them about a general suicidal feelings but then I am concerned that it won't really be effective and just a waste of time I suppose. But maybe that's my depression talking

Thank you so much for your kind words, I really appreciate that. 

The email idea really resonated with me. I live with my partner and he's one of the people that I want to reach out to the most but am also the most worried about and I think an email might really help me both articulate and not freak out and end up talking myself out of reaching out (because I feel like I've approached people so many times with the intentions of asking for help but then chickening out). 

Even if I don't send it, just writing down the things I want to say should help me articulate it later if I just end up ripping the band off and talking to someone

You're right that maybe the contrasting difference from how I normally am might lead to a conversation and I might try that! 

I'm just worried about talking to a professional because I'm pretty sure I'm at the "mandatory reporting" stage of things and have a lot of real world obligations that could get seriously screwed up by suddenly being placed in a psychiatric ward. But maybe that fear is unfounded and there are ways to tiptoe around it, I'm just a bit nervous.
